families.name: Machine Unlearning
families.definition: Techniques that modify trained models to remove specific knowledge or behaviors without full retraining.

properties.text: Methods include gradient ascent on target sequences to induce forgetting.
Some approaches use parametric arithmetic to subtract old knowledge before learning new information.
Ensemble methods like SISA limit the influence of specific data points during training to expedite unlearning.
Techniques can target specific copyrighted content, such as unlearning Harry Potter books from LLMs.
Unlearning can be applied to reduce hallucinations and remove harmful responses.
Some methods use leave-one-out ensembles with teacher-student frameworks to unlearn targeted textual sequences.
Knowledge unlearning via gradient ascent can forget target tokens with little degradation of general language capabilities.

limitations.text: Modifications to the model can alter behavior on key dimensions such as fairness.
It is difficult to verify if all undesirable data has been removed from the training set.
Re-training from scratch is impractical, making unlearning necessary but challenging.
Existing techniques may not suffice for aligned models like ChatGPT without new divergence attacks.
There is a risk that unlearning one piece of information may inadvertently affect other capabilities.

families.name: Model Editing and Knowledge Updating
families.definition: Methods that perform local updates to model weights or parameters to inject new knowledge or correct errors.

properties.text: Task arithmetic uses task vectors to steer model behavior by moving in specific directions in weight space.
Memory-based model editing allows for local updates to inject updated knowledge or correct undesirable behaviors.
Model editors can be used to mitigate biases learned during pre-training.
Parametric arithmetic facilitates the forgetting of old knowledge and learning of new knowledge.
Editing can be used to correct mistakes made by large language models without retraining.

limitations.text: Existing model editors often suffer from insufficient expressiveness.
Editors struggle to accurately model an edit's intended scope, leading to inaccurate predictions for loosely related inputs.
Editors often fail altogether after many edits are applied.
Local updates may not generalize well to broader contexts.

families.name: Bias and Fairness Mitigation
families.definition: Techniques designed to reduce social biases, stereotypes, or unfairness in language model outputs and representations.

properties.text: Zero-shot self-debiasing leverages LLM capabilities to reduce stereotyping without modifying training data or parameters.
Concept erasure methods like LEACE remove specified features from embeddings to improve fairness.
Iterative Null-space Projection (INLP) removes information from neural representations by projecting onto the null-space of linear classifiers.
Some methods disentangle factual gender information from gender bias in model embeddings.
Ensemble post-processing can improve the fairness of unlearning in LLMs.
Data augmentation and filtering methods can decrease stereotypical bias while preserving factual signals.

limitations.text: Most bias mitigation techniques require modifications to training data, model parameters, or decoding strategy.
These modifications may be infeasible without access to a trainable model.
Removing bias can sometimes lead to the loss of factual information, such as grammatical gender.
Biases are deeply embedded in the representations of large language models.

families.name: Privacy Protection and Anonymization
families.definition: Methods that protect sensitive information in textual data or prevent its leakage from models.

properties.text: Deduplicating training data mitigates privacy risks by reducing the superlinear relationship between sequence count and regeneration rate.
Automatic anonymization detects and removes or generalizes sensitive pieces of text in unstructured documents.
Differential privacy techniques can be used to train deep neural networks without exposing private information.
Privacy-preserving mechanisms sanitize data so that identities or confidential attributes are not disclosed.
Document redaction and sanitization models provide privacy guarantees for sensitive document release.

limitations.text: Automatic anonymization of unstructured text is far from being solved.
Textual data protection has received little attention compared to structured databases.
Privacy risks scale with model size, particularly for large language models.
Manual redaction is burdensome and requires human experts.

families.name: Extraction and Membership Inference Attacks
families.definition: Adversarial techniques used to extract training data or determine membership in the training set from language models.

properties.text: Adversaries can extract gigabytes of training data from open-source, semi-open, and closed models.
Divergence attacks can cause aligned models like ChatGPT to diverge from chatbot-style generations to extract data.
Membership inference attacks determine if a specific data record was in the model's training dataset.
Extractable memorization refers to training data that can be efficiently extracted by querying the model.
Attacks can recover personally identifiable information such as names, phone numbers, and email addresses.

limitations.text: Existing techniques may not suffice for unaligned models without new attack strategies.
The success of attacks is largely due to duplication in commonly used web-scraped training sets.
It is difficult to know which problematic data is included in the training set or in what proportions.

families.name: Toxicity and Hallucination Mitigation
families.definition: Methods aimed at reducing the generation of offensive, harmful, or factually incorrect content by language models.

properties.text: Self-detoxifying language models use negative steering prompts to achieve self-detoxification.
Elastic Weight Removal subtracts parameters of a model trained to hallucinate from a dialogue model to negate hallucinated examples.
Quark uses quantized reward conditioning to optimize a reward function that quantifies unwanted properties.
Internet-augmented dialogue generation conditions on search results to reduce hallucinations and provide up-to-date knowledge.
Unlearning can be used to reduce hallucinations as an alignment technique.

limitations.text: Finetuning-based detoxification methods are often resource-intensive.
Decoding-based methods rely on additional components and may compromise generation fluency.
Large language models are prone to generating hallucinations that conflict with source or factual knowledge.
Facts in model weights are frozen in time at the point of model training.
There is currently no way to know which problematic data is included in the training set of large language models or in what proportions.
Automatic anonymization of unstructured text remains far from being solved.
Existing model editors struggle to accurately model an edit's intended scope and often fail after many edits.
It is difficult to verify if all undesirable data has been removed from the training set during unlearning.
Most bias mitigation techniques require access to a trainable model, which may be infeasible for closed-source models.
Privacy risks in machine learning scale with model size, posing a serious threat for large language models.
There is a lack of convincing demonstrations of knowledge use in open-domain dialogue agents.
The underlying cause of privacy risk in machine learning is not well understood beyond anecdotal accounts of overfitting and influence.
